headline.title: We searched "physical therapy Salt Lake City". Pinyon appeared only once, as a Lantern booking page at the very bottom, and we found no website of yours at all.
headline.detail: Hospitals (CommonSpirit, St Mark's, University of Utah), Luna's home PT, Thumbtack and directories took the page. Runners and skiers searching for a PT who gets them back outdoors never meet you.

summary: Pinyon has 98 five-star reviews from ultra-runners, cyclists and skiers who say you explain the root cause and build plans around their goals. But we found no website for you beyond a booking page, and in our search hospitals and directories took almost every spot.

you.notes: Active-people PT; Mon–Thu 7am–7pm; no website found

competitors.name: Intermountain Health Salt Lake Clinic PT

search.result: Hospital pages, Luna (home PT), Thumbtack, Beaming Health and Lantern directories took the results. Pinyon appeared once, as a Lantern booking page in 20th place.
search.meaning: Active people searching for a PT see hospitals and directories, not the clinic their running friends recommend.

visibility: In our search for physical therapy in Salt Lake City, you appeared only through a third-party booking page at the very bottom, and we found no website of yours.
lead: 98 reviews, all five stars, many from serious runners, cyclists and skiers.
Easy online booking with an intake form patients love.
lose: Without a website, people can't see your outdoor-sports focus before booking.
Downtown groups have more reviews and appear in directories.
Hospitals dominate the search for physical therapy.

gaps.title: No website means no first impression
gaps.detail: Athletes research before they trust someone with an injury. Today there's only a booking calendar to find.

gaps.title: Your niche is invisible
gaps.detail: Ultra-running, skiing and climbing rehab is exactly what Salt Lake athletes want, but nothing online says it.

gaps.title: Word of mouth has a ceiling
gaps.detail: Your clients rave about you, but without a site to send friends to, referrals stay small.

actions.title: Launch a website built around outdoor athletes
actions.why: Running, skiing and climbing rehab, with real stories and one-tap booking.

actions.title: Ask every athlete for a review at return-to-sport
actions.why: That's when they're happiest; an automatic message captures it.

actions.title: Complete your Google profile with a website link
actions.why: Doable today once the site exists: it helps you show up in local searches.

plan.title: Your first website with booking built in
plan.detail: Your outdoor-athlete focus, team and stories, with one-tap booking.

plan.title: Automatic review requests
plan.detail: A friendly message after each visit, so happy patients become five-star reviews.

plan.title: Reminders and recall
plan.detail: Follow-up and maintenance reminders that go out by themselves.

plan.title: Your first monthly report
plan.detail: Where you stand against nearby clinics, and what to do next.

scenario: A trail runner in Sugar House strains her Achilles two months before a 50K. She searches "physical therapy Salt Lake City", sees hospital pages and a home-PT service, and books the first slot she finds. She never learns there's a clinic that specialises in getting ultra-runners back on the trail. (Illustration.)
nochange: Your clients keep getting better, but new athletes keep meeting hospitals and directories first. Your best niche stays a secret outside your existing circle.
